contributions.statement: An RL-trained orchestrator rewarded only for task success inflates executor tokens by 24-82% at near-equal accuracy; cost must be an explicit, separately normalized reward.
contributions.evidence: Table 2: w/o cost reward −0.7 to −1.9 points, tokens 6.2→11.3K (math), 3.3→5.7K (embodied), 10.4→12.9K (research).
relative_to: cost-aware RL rewards for agents (e.g. MasRouter, DAAO)

contributions.statement: Plan in milestones: propose one verifiable intermediate goal, plan its subtasks as a DAG, run independent subtasks in parallel, then replan.
contributions.evidence: Table 1 margins 0.7-3.8 points over re-implemented baselines; 16.7-40.4% parallel calls; no coding tasks.

reason: Self-declared WIP whose transferable ideas (milestone planning, cost-aware rewards) are known. The novel part is RL training machinery, which a Java team on hosted agents cannot use. The cost-profile routing it is cited for is tested on two copies of the same 7B model.
